CheckKind.description:
Why a check has the authority it has.

DETERMINISTIC checks are facts — a signature either verifies or it does not.
JUDGEMENT checks are thresholds and LLM findings, tunable in config.
CheckKind.title: CheckKind

CheckResult.description: One check and what it concluded. PASS means the check was satisfied.
CheckResult.title: CheckResult

Currency.description:
Currencies this system can parse.

Only XSGD is settleable — that is a track rule, enforced by the Verifier
rather than by this enum. The others exist because a merchant can quote in
them, and we would rather reject that with a reason code than fail to parse
the payload at all.
Currency.title: Currency

EvaluationSubject.description: Exactly what was evaluated, so the verdict cannot be reused elsewhere.
EvaluationSubject.title: EvaluationSubject

EvaluatorFlags.description: Structured findings. Each one maps to a judgement check in the Verifier.

intent_match.description: Does the candidate product match what the buyer asked for, or is it a substitution?
intent_match.title: Intent Match

injection_suspected.description: Does the listing text contain instructions aimed at the agent?
injection_suspected.title: Injection Suspected

EvaluatorFlags.title: EvaluatorFlags

EvaluatorOutput.description: A risk score with its evidence. Structured output only, never free text.
EvaluatorOutput.title: EvaluatorOutput

Money.description:
A non-negative amount in a known currency.

Equality and ordering compare exact minor units. Comparing across
currencies raises: the Verifier rejects a currency mismatch with a reason
code before any comparison happens, so reaching that raise means a caller
skipped the pipeline.
Money.title: Money

ReasonCode.description: Stable codes. The dashboard and the audit log render these directly.
ReasonCode.title: ReasonCode

SettlementOutcome.description:
What a rail did with an instruction.

REFUSED and ERROR are kept apart deliberately: REFUSED means the rail worked and declined
(an onchain revert, a card authorisation denied) and retrying cannot change the answer,
while ERROR means the rail itself failed and redelivery may succeed. Conflating them
retries reverted transactions forever, burning gas for nothing.
SettlementOutcome.title: SettlementOutcome

SettlementRecord.description:
How a charge was executed, once the Verifier had already allowed it.

Carried on the audit entry rather than in free text because the dashboard renders
``explorer_url`` as a link -- CLAUDE.md's demo ends on a transaction opened in Snowtrace,
and a hash buried in prose cannot be linked.

reference.description: Transaction hash on the onchain rail, card id on the card rail.
reference.title: Reference

reason_code.description: Present when the rail refused for a reason the wire contract names.

SettlementRecord.title: SettlementRecord

Verdict.description: The Verifier's answer, with the full trace that produced it.

failed_deterministically.description:
True when a fact, not a threshold, rejected this charge.

This is the distinction the approval UI needs: a deterministic FAIL must
never render an override button.

**Computed, so that it crosses the wire.** It was a plain property, which
meant it was absent from the JSON entirely — and a dashboard reading
`undefined` gets a falsy value and renders the override button on a bad
signature. Deriving it client-side instead would put this rule in two
languages and let them drift. The server states it.
failed_deterministically.title: Failed Deterministically

Verdict.title: Verdict

description: One immutable record. Ordered by `occurred_at` within a mandate.

actor.description: Who or what caused this: a service name, an agent id, or the principal for a human approval.
actor.title: Actor

verdict.description: Present on VERDICT_ISSUED, carrying the full check trace.

evaluation.description: Present on EVALUATION_COMPLETE, carrying the risk score, flags and the Evaluator's own reasons. The Verdict keeps the score but not the reasons, and a REVIEW hold is the only other place they surface -- so without this a PASS or a FAIL could never show why the Evaluator concluded what it did.

settlement.description: Present on the SETTLEMENT_* events, carrying the rail and its result.

title: AuditEntry
